result:
Understood, no more questions about what you want. One thing comes before the write-up: how it gets built. You've been talking about the brewery, not the software, so I'll make that call. Here are the options so you can overrule me.

**1. Add it to the taproom app (my pick).** Batch tracking becomes a new section of the Flask app already running on the office Pi. It gets its own database file, separate from the tabs. The brewers use it from a tablet in the brewhouse with a handheld barcode scanner, which types the lot number for them. Bottling labels print from the Pi.
- Good: one machine and one app to keep running, and nothing new to buy beyond the scanner.
- Cost: if the Pi goes down, tabs and batch tracking go down together.

**2. A separate app on the same Pi.** It works the same way for the brewers, but runs as its own program.
- Good: a bug in batch tracking can't break the tabs on a busy night.
- Cost: two apps to update and restart. It still runs on one Pi, so it doesn't protect you from the Pi itself failing.

**3. Hosted brewery software.** I'm dropping this one. It's a monthly fee and needs an internet connection in the brewhouse. You'd also be bending your lot-to-label setup to fit its idea of a batch.

I'm going with **option 1**. Keeping the batch data in its own database file means a problem on one side can't corrupt the other.

This is a project-sized piece of work, not a small change, so the design will be a full written document. A reviewer will read it first, and I may come back once with a few questions only you can answer. Then I'll hand you the document. Once you approve it, the next step is planning the build in a fresh session.

If you'd rather go another way, say so now. Otherwise I'll write it up next.
